header: Drive-JEPA 0.1.4b (recorded) vs 0.1.6 (S4 pass-9 weights, bonnet mask, acceleration zeroed) on the 30 census scenes: mean score 0.543 to 0.703; 10 improved, 5 decreased, 15 unchanged; at-fault collisions 4 to 2, none new.

improved.title: Score improved
improved.lead: Ten scenes. In six of them the event that ended or zeroed the 0.1.4b run does not happen under 0.1.6: two at-fault collisions, one off-road exit, two early collisions that were not the car's fault, and one departure from the human path. A seventh, 89f2eeb8, loses its stop. Six of the ten now reach full score.
points: Two of 0.1.4b's four at-fault collisions are gone: 04394343 (was at +2.2 s) and b1b170d0 (was at +0.4 s). Both now run to the end of the clip at full score. No scene gains an at-fault collision.

The hard brake after handover is gone where it mattered. Peak demanded deceleration of the driven plan falls from 18.2 to 1.0 m/s² on 04394343, from 20.7 to 1.0 on b1b170d0 and from 13.2 to 1.3 on 032b6f21, and peak steering falls from 0.76-0.79 rad to 0.01-0.02 rad on all three.
89f2eeb8, the no-cue stop: the stop is gone. 0.1.4b braked to 0.0 m/s by +2.5 s; 0.1.6 never drops below 9.7 m/s and scoring runs to +14.85 s instead of +8.5 s.

bd07fb91 reaches full score without leaving the road, but it still shows a full steering swing (0.78 rad) at +6.5 s, the moment scoring ends; a collision follows at +7.15 s. The score does not see either.

Three gains are partial: 5f064b02 (0.65 to 0.69) and 98dd56b2 (0.16 to 0.34) still end on a collision that is not the car's fault, later than before; d1a25a99 (0.33 to 0.67) still ends early, at +10.45 s.

decreased.title: Score decreased
decreased.lead: Five scenes, none with an at-fault collision or an off-road exit under either version. All five lose progress, for two different reasons.
points: Two leave the human path and the scoring window closes early: e121e37d is 4 m off the path at +9.65 s (it ran the full 16.8 s under 0.1.4b) and cdd9448c at +13.4 s. On e121e37d the car is faster than before (11.1 against 9.4 m/s) when it drifts.

Three drive slower: 1acf2f5d (mean 4.0 against 4.7 m/s), bae463d3 (1.4 against 2.2 m/s, stalled under both) and 0245ff75 (7.5 against 8.0 m/s), where the collision that ends scoring, not the car's fault in either run, comes at +11.0 s instead of +12.9 s.
Four of the five were among 0.1.4b's best scenes (0.86 to 1.00). None has a new at-fault collision.

same.title: No change in score
same.lead: Fifteen scenes. Nine are at full score under both versions. Six fail in the same way under both: three leave the road early, two have the same at-fault collision, one never pulls out.
points: Full score under both (9): five of the nine cover more of the route than before, which the score cannot show because it saturates at 80 % progress (023b7fcc 0.87 to 1.00, 026d6a39 0.84 to 1.00, 02eadd92 0.82 to 1.00, 048b974e 0.84 to 1.00, 6725df2d 0.89 to 1.00).

Highway, 04749bb9 and acd22430: both still leave the road with a full steering swing (0.78 rad). 04749bb9 gets past the first second (off the road at +2.7 s instead of +0.4 s) and holds 18-22 m/s for three seconds; acd22430 is off the road at +0.25 s. The first plan now asks for 5-7 m/s² of braking instead of 14-17, and the plan half a second later asks for 12.

Pull-outs, d2715023 and b44a4a44: neither moves. Plans that leave are on the menu at every replan (a median of 21 and 24 of the 32), but the scorer's best-ranked one sits at rank 9 to 12 of 32 and is never picked.
8023dce5 has the same at-fault collision, later (+7.2 s instead of +4.1 s). 791d68ce is off the road from the handover under both.
